text: Every loop can be rewritten as a recursive method, and every recursive method as a loop.
explanation: This is Chapter 13's equivalence, and it is why Chapter 25's interpreted language needs no loop construct at all — `fact` iterates by recursing, and the language is still Turing complete. The practical asymmetry is that the mechanical rewrite from recursion to iteration is easy only for tail recursion; a tree recursion generally needs an explicit stack, which is Chapter 12's stack made visible in your own code.
